facts.text: Manzano’s name comes from the Spanish word for 'apple tree,' reflecting the region’s historic apple orchards.
The Quarai Ruins of Salinas Pueblo Missions National Monument sit just outside Manzano, offering a glimpse into ancient Pueblo life.
Spanish colonists in the early 1800s turned Manzano into a mission town, with the Catholic Church guiding land grants and settlement.
Between 1100 and 1300, Tompiro and Tiwa peoples built stone villages on Manzano Mountain’s eastern slopes, creating a thriving prehistoric trade hub.
Late 17th‑century droughts and raids forced both Indigenous peoples and Spanish settlers to abandon homes, sparking Manzano’s decline.
Manzano’s cultural tourism spotlights the blend of Tiwa, Tompiro, and Spanish mission heritage, drawing visitors to historic ruins and mission‑era architecture.
